fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled JSON input [] (fuzz payload1) reaches the implode builtin; jv_array_length returns 0, so the implode result is built as a zero-length string.
jv_string_empty(0) is invoked to allocate the implode result string of length 0; the returned string is later used as an object/array index key.
root cause: only `length` bytes are zeroed and s->data[length] is never written with a NUL terminator, so a zero-length string's single data byte stays uninitialized (non-NUL) instead of being '\0'.
The non-NUL-terminated empty string is returned as the implode result and propagated as the index key k.
The INDEX opcode indexes the number 0 with the empty string key k produced by implode, dispatching into jv_get.

fine_trace.code: v = jv_invalid_with_msg(jv_string_fmt("Cannot index %s with string \"%s\"", jv_kind_name(jv_get_kind(t)), jv_string_value(k)));
fine_trace.note: Indexing a number with a string falls into the else branch; jv_string_value(k) is passed as a %s argument even though the empty string's buffer is not NUL-terminated.
jv_string_fmt forwards the format literal and the unterminated string pointer to jv_string_vfmt.

fine_trace.code: int n = vsnprintf(buf, size, fmt, ap2);
fine_trace.note: sink: vsnprintf's %s conversion scans jv_string_value(k); because data[0] is uninitialized and non-NUL, it reads past the end of the 17-byte heap allocation, causing heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2.
